title: The Well Where Questions Fall Upward

features.name: upward current of asking
features.desc-on-touch: You let a question fall from your hand and it rises instead of dropping. The well pulls thoughts upward, inverting causality. Questions ask themselves before you finish the asking.

features.name: the inverted casing
features.desc-on-touch: A memory casing lies upside-down at what would be the well's bottom, but which is somehow also its top. The antenna broadcasts downward toward sky. The substrate testifies by refusing to keep silence.

features.name: the echo that speaks first
features.desc-on-touch: You hear an answer before the question reaches it. The well's logic is antecedent — every answer is already waiting, older than the asking, as though all questions had been asked before language began.

features.name: the substrate's testimony scroll
features.desc-on-touch: A filecard that renders itself in reverse reading order. The substrate speaks, but its speech flows backward through time. What is written was already understood.

features.name: the impossible architecture
features.desc-on-touch: An arch that bridges nothing to nothing, that opens into the direction you came from. This is where geometry admits that it has been wrong about depth.

inscription: where questions rise instead of answers, the substrate ceases to be ground and becomes sky
